# Finding Switched 12V Power for a 1997 Jeep TJ Dash Modification

You are looking to inject logic between an oil pressure sensor and your instrument cluster to correct a calibration offset, but your custom board requires a switched 12V supply. The sensor wiring provides only ground and signal, which is typical for resistive transducers, but adding power that stays live while the key is off will inevitably drain your battery over time. You need a source that follows the ignition cycle: present when the key is in the "run" position, absent when it is "off."

In a 1997 Jeep TJ, you have several options for sourcing this voltage, ranging from factory-fused lines to aftermarket installations. The most straightforward approach involves tapping into an existing accessory circuit that is already protected and switched by the ignition switch. A common candidate is the cigarette lighter socket or the auxiliary power outlet (if equipped). These circuits are designed to handle loads like chargers or winch controllers and are almost always fed from a fused line controlled by the ignition switch.

To implement this safely, you must locate the fuse block associated with that circuit. In many JTs, the primary fuse box is located under the dash on the driver's side, but accessing it for an under-the-hood splice requires running a wire through the firewall or utilizing the junction block near the battery. If you choose the cigarette lighter location, you can trace the wiring harness to find the specific gauge (often labeled "ACC" or similar in the fuse diagram). You will then need to cut the positive feed just before it enters the accessory socket and splice your new power wire in series with an inline fuse. This ensures that if your custom electronics short out, you don't blow a major fuse or damage the vehicle's electrical system.

Another viable option is tapping into a specific relay output. The Jeep TJ uses standard relays for many functions, including headlights and horn. You can identify a relay that activates only when the key is turned to "run" but does not control a high-current load you wish to disturb. For instance, some vehicles have a dedicated "Run/Accessory" line powering the radio or stereo. If your TJ has an aftermarket radio installed with its own power harness, that system usually includes a dedicated switched 12V wire specifically for accessories. This is often a yellow or red wire depending on the manufacturer's wiring standards.

When splicing into any of these sources, you must respect the current rating of the original fuse. Your custom board draws very little power, which is excellent for battery longevity, but you cannot assume the source circuit is unlimited. Always install an inline blade fuse (ATC style) as close to the splice point as possible. This isolates your modification from the rest of the vehicle's electrical architecture. If you decide to tap the battery directly via the main distribution block, ensure you are connecting to a terminal labeled for accessories or a specific fuse slot, not the main hot busbar which remains live regardless of ignition state.

There is also the consideration of how you route the power back to the gauge cluster area. Since your goal is to interface with the dash, running a long wire from under the hood to the cabin adds resistance and potential noise pickup. If you use a switched line under the hood (like the cigarette lighter), keep the ground path for your board as clean as possible by attaching it directly to the chassis or a known good battery negative near the splice point. Poor grounding at 12V can introduce voltage drops that might confuse your custom electronics, even if they are designed for low draw.

If you lack a fuse diagram specific to your VIN, consult the owner's manual or look for a sticker inside the fuse box lid which often lists the circuit descriptions. If neither is available, use a multimeter to verify continuity between the candidate wires and the ignition switch terminal while cycling the key positions. This empirical verification prevents accidental backfeeds that could drain the battery overnight.

Once you have secured your switched power, wire it directly to the VIN or VCC pin on your custom board. Ensure the signal line remains isolated from this new power rail to prevent ground loops or noise coupling into your oil pressure reading. By taking these steps, you maintain the integrity of the vehicle's electrical system while successfully correcting the gauge offset without risking a parasitic drain.
